body: Australia has canceled, or rather paused, its planned purchase of a fourth squadron of Lockheed Martin F-35 Lightning II fighter jets. The country has received all 72 F-35s it committed to, against a program of record for 100 aircraft, with the final jet arriving in December 2024. That makes Australia the largest export customer for the F-35 in the world, ahead of the United Kingdom, which has received around 44 of its 48 contracted examples.

In April 2024, Australian Aviation reported that the federal government had put on hold plans to buy a fourth squadron of F-35s and would instead redirect some of that investment towards long-range missiles. The decision followed a plan to upgrade the existing Super Hornet fleet and keep it flying into the 2040s, rather than retiring it by around 2027 as previously intended. Australia now operates three F-35 squadrons alongside 24 F/A-18 Super Hornets and 12 EA-18G Growlers.

Australian Defence Industry Minister Pat Conroy gave two main reasons for keeping the Super Hornets and delaying the fourth F-35 squadron. One was that the Super Hornets were "doing great work." The second, he said, was that the "Joint Strike Fighter [F-35] is even more capable than we initially thought." The door remains open: in March 2025, the Coalition pledged to acquire more F-35s to reach 100 aircraft if it won the federal election, but it lost, and the Labor Government returned to power. Australia announced in 2025 that it was actively exploring involvement in the Tempest/GCAP sixth-generation program, scheduled to enter service in 2035 and seen as a potential replacement for its Super Hornets.
en.summary: Australia has received all 72 of its committed F-35s but has paused plans for a fourth squadron, extending its Super Hornets into the 2040s and redirecting funds to long-range missiles, while leaving the door open to future purchases or next-generation aircraft.
en.title: Australia pauses its fourth F-35 squadron as Super Hornets fly into the 2040s

body: 澳洲已取消、更精確地說是暫緩第四個F-35中隊的採購計畫。澳洲在其總數100架的計畫中已承諾採購72架F-35，且已全數接收，最後一架於2024年12月抵達，使澳洲成為全球最大的F-35出口客戶，領先已接收約44架的英國。F-35目前已在澳洲全面投入運作，構成該國戰機戰力的骨幹。
2024年4月，《澳洲航空》報導聯邦政府已暫緩採購第四個F-35中隊，並將部分投資轉向長程飛彈。做出這項決定之前，澳洲決定升級現有超級大黃蜂機隊並使其服役至2040年代，而非如原先計畫約於2027年退役。澳洲目前擁有3個F-35中隊，另有24架F/A-18超級大黃蜂與12架EA-18G咆哮者，延後退役可釋出資金，用於採購更多長程飛彈與其他系統。

澳洲國防工業部長Pat Conroy當時提出兩個主要理由：一是超級大黃蜂表現出色，二是F-35的能力超出最初預期，因此澳洲目前不認為需要再多採購F-35來達到所需戰力。未來仍有變數：2025年3月，聯盟黨承諾若贏得聯邦大選將增購F-35至100架，但在大選中落敗，工黨政府留任；澳洲並於2025年宣布積極探索參與Tempest/GCAP次世代戰機計畫，該機預定2035年服役，被視為超級大黃蜂的潛在替代選項，第四個F-35中隊的大門仍未關上。
zh.summary: 澳洲已接收全部72架承諾採購的F-35，成為全球最大F-35出口客戶，但聯邦政府暫緩採購第四個中隊；超級大黃蜂將延壽至2040年代，省下的資金轉向長程飛彈與其他系統，未來仍可能回頭採購或轉向次世代戰機。
zh.title: 澳洲暫緩第四個F-35中隊：超級大黃蜂延壽至2040年代，資金轉向長程飛彈
